CHM5716.title: Materials Chemistry (FAU) / Characterization of Materials I (FSU)
CHM5716.prerequisites: Graduate course; carriers use the number for DIFFERENT COURSES. FAU (Materials Chemistry, 3 cr): graduate students in the College of Science or Engineering; dual-numbered with undergraduate CHM 4714 (prereq CHM 2210), so ask before registering if you took CHM 4714. FSU (Characterization of Materials I): none listed; 3 credits in the 2026-27 bulletin but 1 in the state file; repeatable in the same term to 9 credits. Preparation either way: undergraduate inorganic and physical chemistry. The statewide title "Topics in Materials Chemistry II" is a deleted FSU entry and matches neither course. FAU's course corresponds to FSU's CHM 5715. Send the syllabus on transfer, not the number.

offering_notes.summary: Two public carriers, both graduate, teaching different courses under one number: a solid-state materials chemistry survey at FAU and a characterization-methods course at FSU. Both list 3 credits in their own catalogs; the state course file records FSU at 1 credit. Neither publishes contact hours.
offering_notes.derivation: Florida's convention of 45 contact hours for a 3-credit lecture course. FAU's graduate students also attend crystallography workshop sessions outside lecture.

offerings.title: Materials Chemistry
offerings.note: Introduction to solid-state and inorganic materials chemistry, particularly X-ray diffraction; crystallography workshop included. Graduate students in the College of Science or Engineering. Dual-numbered with undergraduate CHM 4714 (same description, prerequisite CHM 2210). Text in the 2013 proposal: Smart and Moore, Solid State Chemistry: An Introduction.

offerings.title: Characterization of Materials I
offerings.note: Microscopic and diffraction methods for structural characterization, plus transport and magnetic measurements; recommended for materials researchers. Repeatable within the same term to 9 credit hours. 3 credits in the 2026-27 FSU bulletin; the state course file carries it at 1 credit (since 2009). FSU's materials survey is CHM 5715, not this number.
